changes.why: A definition hall should let the visitor fail to predict at the measured rate — an experiment the text initiates and the room already affords.
changes.before: One destination, then another, with a slowing and setting off between them. Behind the bead, pale circles begin to cover one another.
changes.after:
One destination, then another, with a slowing and setting off between them. Behind the bead, pale circles begin to cover one another.

We try calling each departure before it happens. Some calls land; counted along the rod, no more of them than luck would explain. That failure can be measured, and it is the first measurement this room offers.

changes.why: The everyday misdefinition — random means no runs — belongs in the definition hall. Most five-digit groups hold a repeat (~70%); RAND's correctors worked against bias, not repetition.
changes.before: The falling digits here are generated by this exhibit, not lifted from RAND's tables.
changes.after:
The falling digits here are generated by this exhibit, not lifted from RAND's tables.

Most of the passing groups hold a repeated digit somewhere. Nothing has gone wrong. A table from which the doubles had been combed out would be a doctored table — RAND's correctors worked against bias, not against repetition. What chance is not allowed to do is look the way we expect it to.

changes.why: Random_Entropy, the next hall, is titled 'What the gauge forgets' — the bit extraction is its opening argument and inherits r1's bits vocabulary with it. What stays funds the chapter's one definitional move, which the room demonstrates three times and never names.
changes.before:
The cabinet has another way of reading the intervals. It compares pairs of gaps to produce bits, zeros or ones. We keep the ninety-six events fixed and make the comparison clock coarser, measuring in larger steps. Two gaps that had different durations may now receive the same measured value. Such a pair is skipped. Nothing disappears from the timeline or the sound. One procedure has lost a distinction that another record still holds.

We can hear the gaps once more. For this comparison, the tied pair still yields no bit.
changes.after:
The cabinet can also read its own intervals against a coarser clock, measuring in larger steps. Two gaps of different lengths may then receive the same measured value, and a distinction the sound still carries goes missing from that account. Nothing in the gaps has changed — only the resources brought to them.

That is the definition this room has been circling. Random is not a property a sequence owns. It is a relation between the sequence and whatever meets it: a clock, a rule, a listener. The same ninety-six times are a riddle to our ear and a recipe to the generator.

changes.why: Hall one of fourteen must hand off. The door opens; the room still closes on the original last line. 'A rule it did not write' carries E's constitution at the dose this voice holds.
